blocks.text: This chapter explains how the Shaddad digital twin is organised. It covers which models exist and how they are nested, how a command travels from the operator's sticks to the tracks and back, the rate each part runs at, and which switches (variant controls) select the phase, the fidelity and the target. Read it before opening the models, because later chapters use the names introduced here. The binding sources are `docs/architecture.md` (decisions D1-D63) and the generated interface control document `docs/icd.md`. If this chapter disagrees with those files, the files are correct.
Architecture at a glance

The model divides the robot into three kinds of parts. **Embedded controllers** are modelled as firmware that can be code-generated: the STM32H743 main controller (MCU), the STM32G4 battery management ECU (BMS) and, in Phase 2, the companion computer. The **physical plant** is a set of Simscape networks for structure, power, drive and electronics hardware. **Simulation infrastructure** replaces the world around the robot: the operator and RC link, the CAN networks, the sensor models, the monitors and the visualisation. {fig:F18_architecture.png} shows the Phase 1 architecture, and {tab:tab_layers} maps each layer to its model file.

blocks.text: Phase concept

One model serves both project phases. In **Phase 1** the operator drives Shaddad by remote control: SBUS frames from the transmitter reach the MCU, which decodes, maps, shapes and mixes them into speed commands for the two traction ESCs. **Phase 2** adds autonomy: a companion computer runs navigation, perception and guidance and sends velocity commands to the MCU over CAN-FD. The base-workspace scalar `VC_PHASE` selects the phase by switching the Variant Subsystem `Shaddad_System/GNC_Variant` ({tab:tab_phases}).

blocks.text: The MCU always has final authority over the mode. RC stick override, the MANUAL switch position, the remote E-stop (CH12) and every supervisor fault override GNC commands. The hardware E-stop chain in `Power_Plant/Safety_Chain` works independently of all firmware. In Phase 1 the AUTO position of the mode switch (CH5) cannot arm AUTO, because AUTO entry requires an arm edge plus `comp_ok` and `gnc_ready` from a companion that is not present.

Scenarios set `VC_PHASE` themselves with `Simulink.SimulationInput.setVariable`. For example, `scn_S1_rc_drive` uses 1 and `scn_S5_palm_obstacles` uses 2, so the result of `run_scenario` and `phase1_test_drive` does not depend on the base-workspace value. Both phases compile with 0 algebraic loops. A full update in a fresh MATLAB session took 84 s for Phase 1 and 62 s for Phase 2 in the acceptance run (before the fix pass, `docs/STATUS.md` 5.1).
Top model and model hierarchy

`models/Shaddad_System.slx` is the top model ({fig:F01_system_top_overview.png}). It contains no Simscape blocks. Every functional block and its ports are defined in ICD section 3.1, and the signal lines carry the names used there. The build script adds helper blocks that the ICD does not list: Signal Specifications, Bus Selectors, Terminators and the loop-breaking Unit Delays. {tab:tab_top} lists the blocks; its numbers are the callouts in {fig:F01_system_top_overview.png}, {fig:F01_system_top_detail.png} and {fig:F17_simulink_editor_callouts.png}.

blocks.text: Model blocks and Subsystem References

The hierarchy uses two kinds of referenced file. The rule (architecture section 5) is simple. Code-generated controllers are **Model References**. Everything physical or on the plant side is a **Subsystem Reference (SSR)**. {tab:tab_mtypes} lists the files.

blocks.caption: Model files and their kind
rows: All Simscape networks and the Solver Configuration
Companion navigation, perception and guidance, inside `Shaddad_Companion`
Subsystem References (117 files, including the two generated battery libraries and the HW-only model `companion_io_ros2`)
Plant domains, firmware units `fw_*`, CAN codecs, RC link, sensors, monitors

items: **Model blocks for ECUs.** Each ECU model compiles as a separate unit. Its root ports are nonvirtual buses, each port carries one rate, and every port declares an explicit, non-constant sample time. Code generation needs exactly this contract: the file that runs in the system simulation is the same file that Embedded Coder would build for the STM32H743, the STM32G4 or the ROS 2 companion. A Model block also keeps its own compiled target (the `.slxc` files in `work/`).

**Subsystem References for physics.** Simscape physical connections cannot cross a Model-block boundary. Every Simscape network (structure, power, drive, electronics hardware) is therefore an SSR, and all of them sit together inside the single plant model `Shaddad_Plant`, so no physical line leaves that model (D14). At compile time an SSR is expanded into its parent: it shares the parent's solver and rates, and it can expose physical Connection Ports.

**The plant is also a Model block**, although it is never code-generated. Wrapping the expensive Simscape part in a Model Reference gives it a cached compiled target and a signal-only interface to the rest of the system: 6 inputs and 17 outputs (ICD 3.2).

**Firmware units are SSRs inside the ECU models.** The MCU firmware is assembled from SSR units (`fw_sbus_decoder`, `fw_rc_mapping`, `fw_safety_supervisor`, `fw_mode_manager`, `fw_vehicle_ctrl` and others), so each unit can be tested in its own bench. The ESC firmware model `drive_esc` is an SSR inside the plant, because it represents the firmware of a commercial ESC and is never generated.

**State machines** are MATLAB Function blocks with uint8 enumerations, written as ordered transition tables (for example `mcu_mode_manager.m`, `bms_mode_manager.m`, `esc_sm.m`), because Stateflow is not installed (architecture decision D1). The function bodies live in `.m` files on the project path.

blocks.text: The plant model

`Shaddad_Plant` ({fig:F02_plant_top.png}) contains `Plant_In` and four domain SSRs: `Structure` (`structure_plant`), `Power` (`Power_Plant`), `Drive` (`drive_system`) and `Electronics` (`Electronics_Plant`). `Plant_In` re-times the scenario signals (body HMI and faults from 10 ms to 1 ms, environment overrides from 10 ms to 100 ms) and maps the drive fault injection. Zero-Order Holds sample the continuous plant outputs at the declared port rates: truth and track state at 1 ms, structure diagnostics at 10 ms. The domains are coupled by the physical connections in {tab:tab_pports}.

The traction and LV network has exactly one Solver Configuration, on line `DC48_TracL_n` at the plant top level, and one Electrical Reference inside `Power_Plant/PDU` at the ground node after the shunt. The enclosure thermal network `Electronics_Plant/Electronics_Thermal` has no external ports and therefore has its own Solver Configuration (0.1 s). Variant choices without a motor (for example `Impl_None` or the ideal drive plant) contain a network tie, so every mechanical and thermal node stays connected to the DC48 network in every variant combination (D35).

blocks.text: Signal flow in Phase 1
The steps below trace one RC command through the model and back. The block names match {fig:F01_system_top_overview.png} (numbers in {tab:tab_top}) and {fig:F02_plant_top.png}.

items: **Operator.** `ScenarioIn.op` (`Bus_OperatorCmd`, 10 ms) carries stick positions and switch states. `Operator_Console` passes it on, or substitutes the dashboard values, as `op` (`VC_OPSRC`).

**RC link.** `RC_Link_Sim` converts the sticks into 16 channels (raw 172..1811, centre 992), applies radio frame loss and the receiver failsafe, encodes a 25-byte SBUS frame every 14 ms, and emits the bytes with 100 kbaud 8E2 timing as `Bus_SbusStream`: up to 32 bytes per 1 ms tick plus a UART error flag.
**MCU input.** `MCU_In` re-times every input to its task rate and builds `Bus_McuIn1k` ... `Bus_McuIn100`.

**MCU firmware.** Task_1k decodes SBUS (`fw_sbus_decoder` with the frame synchroniser `sbus_frame_sync.m`) and supervises the link. Task_10 maps the channels (`fw_rc_mapping`), evaluates the 32-bit fault word (`fw_safety_supervisor`), runs the mode state machine (`fw_mode_manager`) and runs vehicle control (`fw_vehicle_ctrl`: arbitration, speed and yaw shaping, yaw-rate PI on the IMU gyro, skid-steer mixing, torque limits). `CAN1_Codec` packs the result into DRV_CMD_L/R (0x201/0x202).
**CAN1.** `CAN1_Net_Sim` delivers the frames ({tab:tab_can1}) to the plant input `can_mcu_fast`. Faults can be injected on the way (frame drop, bus-off).

**Drive.** In `drive_system`, `drive_cmd_unpack` decodes each frame, a Rate Transition moves it from 10 ms to 1 ms, and each `drive_side` closes the 1 kHz speed loop in the ESC model `drive_esc`. The ESC drives the PMSM, the 24:1 gearbox and the spring brake, and the gearbox output turns the sprocket port `Spr_L` or `Spr_R`.
**Structure.** `structure_plant` computes the track-soil forces and the 6-DOF chassis motion, and exports `Bus_TruthState` (ENU/FLU) at 1 ms.

**Power.** `Power_Plant` supplies the DC link from the 16S3P pack through the PDU. `Safety_Chain` drives the safe-torque-off input (`safety_ok`) of both ESCs. `Power_Sensors` sends `Bus_BMS_Meas` to the BMS, which returns contactor, balancing and fan commands (`Bus_BMS_Cmd`) and its CAN frames.

**Feedback.** The ESC frames DRV_FB1/FB3 (10 ms) and FB2 (50 ms), the implement ECU frame and the BMS frames (100 ms) return over CAN1 to the MCU. The IMU model output `Bus_ImuRaw` (5 ms) reaches Task_5. The electronics front end returns the digital input word (E-stop channels, bumpers, reset button) at 1 ms.

**MCU outputs to hardware.** The DO word (`out1k`, including DO0 MCU_SAFETY_OK and the DO1 re-arm pulse) and the PWM duties (`out10`) go to `Electronics_Plant`. It decodes them into the safety-chain signals (DO0, re-arm pulse), the K3 24 V implement relay request and the sprayer and lift actuator commands for the power plant, implement commands for the structure, and LV load demand. The contactors K1, K2 and K4 are commanded by the BMS (`Bus_BMS_Cmd`), not by the MCU.

blocks.text: CAN1 is classic CAN 2.0B at 500 kbit/s with 11-bit IDs (STM32 FDCAN1), at a bus load of about 21 %. Each ECU packs and unpacks its own frames with `Byte Pack`/`Byte Unpack` in the logic shared by the SIM and HW variants, so every simulation exercises the codecs (D6). An ESC enters QUICK_STOP after 100 ms without a new DRV_CMD alive value. The MCU raises DRV_x_TIMEOUT after 50 ms without FB1/FB3.
Multirate scheme

Everything except the Simscape networks and a few continuous states in the structure model is discrete. Every task and port rate must be in the allowed set **{1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 200, 1000} ms**, and `shaddad_params` stops with an error if any named sample time is outside it. The SBUS frame period of 14 ms (7 ms in the high-speed option) exists only inside `RC_Link_Sim`. {tab:tab_rates} shows what runs at each rate.

blocks.text: Deterministic rate transitions

items: Every rate change is an explicit `Rate Transition` block with Integrity on, Deterministic on and a specified output sample time. With `AutoInsertRateTranBlk = off` and `MultiTaskRateTransMsg = error`, a missing transition stops the compile; Simulink never inserts one silently.

A deterministic transfer requires an integer ratio between the two rates. Non-integer pairs such as 10 ms and 14 ms are chained through 1 ms: inside `RC_Link_Sim` the path is 0.01 -> 0.001 -> 0.014 s, and the frame leaves the block at 0.001 s (D32).

A fast-to-slow transfer adds no delay. A slow-to-fast transfer adds one slow period in multitasking. That period is the modelled transport latency (for example 10 ms from the MCU to the ESC) and is never relied on to break an algebraic loop.
Nonvirtual buses that cross a Model-block boundary carry one rate each. This is why the MCU has five input buses and six output buses.

`utilities/shaddad_rate_audit.m` compiles the hierarchy and checks every compiled sample time against `P.sim.Ts_compiled_allowed` (0, Inf, the allowed set, 0.007 and 0.014 s). The values 0.007 and 0.014 s are accepted only inside `Operator_RC`.

blocks.text: Explicit loop breakers

A Simscape network with a local solver acts as direct feedthrough, and the output function of a referenced model is monolithic. Feedback between Model blocks would therefore form algebraic loops. Explicit Unit Delays break every such loop, and each one represents a real sampling or compute delay (D36). {tab:tab_delays} lists the delays in the top model. Inside the plant, 1 ms delays sit on the ESC-to-plant commands, on the belt speed in the track-shear damping and on the implement load-torque inputs. In Phase 2, `Link_MCU_GNC` delays MCU_STATUS by one 50 ms sample. The system compiles with `AlgebraicLoopMsg = error` and has 0 algebraic loops.

blocks.text: Latency budget of the RC command path

The rate structure sets the RC latency (D37). **TX frame to DRV_CMD:** 14 ms frame period + 3 ms byte transfer + up to 1 ms poll + up to 10 ms Task_10 phase gives 18-28 ms against a 30 ms limit, and S1 measured 28 ms. **Operator stick to ESC speed reference:** the input transition (+10 ms), the frame phase (0-14 ms) and the ESC transition (+10 ms) give 38-62 ms against a 65 ms limit, and S1 measured 50 ms. **RF loss to controlled stop:** at most 0.13 s (0.10 s link timeout + 14 + 3 + 1 + 10 ms).
Variant controls

Variant controls are plain double scalars in the base workspace, created by `shaddad_params`. They are scalars because variant expressions cannot index structs. Every variant uses activation time *update diagram*: a new `VC_*` value takes effect at the next update or compile, and inactive choices are not compiled. {tab:tab_vc_arch} lists all variant controls.

blocks.text: `shaddad_params('Phase', 2, 'Implement', 1, 'Target', 0)` sets `VC_PHASE`, `VC_IMPL` and `VC_TARGET` together with the matching parameters. For batch runs, pass variant values with `Simulink.SimulationInput.setVariable`, as `scn_base_input` does, instead of editing the base workspace. `VC_OPSRC = 3` is only a constant placeholder (transmitter on, sticks neutral, disarmed), because `vrlib/Joystick Input` is not available in R2026b on this installation.
Buses and interface control

Every signal interface is typed by a `Simulink.Bus` object. `buses/shaddad_buses.m` creates all **88 buses** in the base workspace from seven per-domain definition files ({tab:tab_buses}). Each domain owns one file, so builders working in parallel never edit the same file.

items: **Naming.** Every bus name starts with `Bus_` (checked when the buses are created), and element names are unique within a bus. Each element carries `Unit` and `Description`, and many also carry Min/Max limits.

**Per-rate root buses.** The root I/O of a Model block is split by rate: `Bus_McuIn1k`, `Bus_McuIn5`, `Bus_McuIn10`, `Bus_McuIn50`, `Bus_McuIn100` and the matching `Bus_McuOut*`. Buses at Model boundaries are nonvirtual (`BusOutputAsStruct = on`).

**CAN frames as slot buses.** `Bus_CanFrame8` (`id`, `len`, `data[8]`, `valid`) carries a classic CAN frame and `Bus_CanFrame64` a CAN-FD frame. Slots are grouped by producer and rate, for example `Bus_Can1_McuFast`, `Bus_Can1_EscFast`, `Bus_Can1_Bms`.
**Enumerations.** 15 uint8 enumeration classes in `buses/` (for example `ShaddadMode`: 0 BOOT ... 9 FAULT) are used inside the models. Buses carry the uint8 code.
**Units.** SI on every bus. Temperatures are in K except fields suffixed `_degC`, and angles are in rad except fields suffixed `_deg`.

blocks.text: **Initial conditions.** `buses/bus_ic.m` builds an initial-condition struct for every bus in `P.ic.Bus_<Name>`. It has the same field order, sizes and classes as `Simulink.Bus.createMATLABStruct` and is about 1000 times faster. Values are zero, except that an element whose range excludes zero gets the bound nearest to zero (for example `Bus_EnvState.T_amb` = 233.15 K), so the initial condition passes Simulink's range check. Every Constant, Unit Delay and Rate Transition that carries a bus uses these structs, and so do the stubs: `GNC_Stub` outputs `P.ic.<Bus>`.

**ICD.** `utilities/shaddad_icd_report.m` generates `docs/icd.md` from two sources: the hand-written sections in `docs/icd_static_sections.md` (conventions, ports, CAN maps, I/O maps, RC channel map, variants, enumerations) and the bus definitions (section 10, every element). Regenerate the ICD after any bus change, and never edit `icd.md` directly.

names = shaddad_buses();             % create the 88 Bus_* objects in the base workspace
rep   = shaddad_buses('check');      % resolve nested types, createMATLABStruct on every bus
shaddad_icd_report();                % regenerate docs/icd.md
n     = shaddad_check_interfaces();  % root ports of every file vs. the wiring contract (0 = all match)
Parameters: P, Ts and P_meta

`params/shaddad_params.m` runs at project startup. It assembles the parameter struct `P`, the sample-time struct `Ts`, the descriptive-string struct `P_meta`, the `VC_*` scalars and the `Bus_*` objects, and writes them to the base workspace ({tab:tab_params}).

37 named sample times, for example `Ts.base` 1 ms, `Ts.imu` 5 ms, `Ts.ctrl` 10 ms, `Ts.comm` 50 ms, `Ts.hk` 100 ms, `Ts.mcmd` 0.2 s, `Ts.rc_frame` 14 ms

items: `P` holds only numeric and logical values, so every field is tunable and safe for code generation. Strings live in `P_meta`, which no block references (D58).
MATLAB Function blocks receive sub-structs (for example `P.electronics.safety`), never the whole of `P`.

The assembly order follows the data dependencies: buses -> sim/frames -> world -> power -> structure (needs the battery mass) -> drive (needs the sprocket radius) -> electronics -> rc -> sensors -> gnc -> `P.ic`.

Cross-domain assertions stop the assembly when the data is inconsistent. They check that drive and structure use the same sprocket radius, electronics and drive the same gear ratio, sensors and world the same datum, the pack energy matches the GNC value, the track gauge factor chi comes from one source, the GNC command envelope stays inside the MCU limits, the ESC ramp never limits an MCU deceleration, the motor peak torque fits the gearbox rating, the receiver failsafe preset cannot command the remote E-stop, `VC_DRIVE_FID` is not the bench-only FOC choice, and HV_LOST has a persistence time.
Every `Ts` field except `rc_frame` must belong to `P.sim.Ts_allowed`, and `rc_frame` must be 0.007 or 0.014 s.
The simulation configuration sets use `DefaultParameterBehavior = Tunable`. A value change therefore does not rebuild the model targets, but a dimension or variant change does.

Coordinate frames and sign conventions

{tab:tab_frames} lists the conventions, which bind every bus (ICD 1) and follow ROS REP-103. When you read a plot or write a scenario, the two rules that matter most are: **yaw is measured from East, counter-clockwise positive**, and **a positive yaw rate is a left turn**.

blocks.text: Solver configuration

Every model carries the configuration reference `Shaddad_Ref`, which points to the base-workspace variable `cs_Shaddad`. At startup, `shaddad_configsets('fixed')` creates `cs_Shaddad` and the other sets, so one variable controls the solver settings of all models. {tab:tab_solver} compares the default set with the accuracy reference.

blocks.caption: Simulation configuration sets
rows: Local solver on each Solver Configuration: Backward Euler, 1 ms (enclosure network 0.1 s), fixed cost, MaxNonlinIter 3, MaxModeIter 2
Algebraic loops, rate transitions and bus-as-vector: error; unconnected inputs: warning

blocks.text: A fixed 1 ms step matches the fastest discrete rate (the 1 kHz MCU and ESC tasks). Fixed-cost local Backward Euler solvers keep the cost of each step deterministic and remain stable for the stiff electrical parts, such as the 41 µs contactor inrush and the 30 µs DC-link time constant, even though 1 ms under-resolves them. The remaining Simulink continuous states (6-DOF body, track shear) must have eigenvalues of at most 1000 1/s for `ode3` at 1 ms; the worst case in the structure model is about 400 1/s. The code-generation sets `cs_GenARM`, `cs_STM32H7`, `cs_STM32G4` and `cs_Companion` (inlined parameters) also exist, but every build with them is blocked while Simulink Coder is not installed.

Run in Normal mode. Windows Application Control blocks the Accelerator and Rapid Accelerator MEX files on this PC, so use `'Mode','normal'` (`phase1_test_drive` does this). The Phase 1 real-time factor is about 0.3-0.5. MATLAB memory grows with every compile; see {sec:ch08_user_manual/PC requirements}.

The reference-solver mode `run_scenario(id, 'Solver', 'ref')` currently stops with a data-integrity error in `Electronics_Thermal` (`docs/STATUS.md`, open problem 12). Use the default fixed-step set for all runs in this report.
SIM and HW variants

One global switch, `VC_TARGET`, selects simulation (0) or target hardware (1). In each code-generated model, the hardware boundary is a pair of Variant Subsystems, `IO_In` and `IO_Out`, with activation at update diagram ({tab:tab_target}).

rows: `fw_io_in_hw` / `fw_io_out_hw`: USART2 UART Read (SBUS), GPIOF Digital Port Read, ICM-20948 on I2C1, FDCAN1/FDCAN2 Read and Write (raw data), ADC1 and ADC3, PWM on TIM1/TIM4, GPIOG/GPIOE Digital Port Write, register access to TIM2 CNT, RCC_RSR, FDCAN PSR and IWDG1

items: The SIM buses reproduce the driver-block outputs exactly, so the downstream logic cannot tell SIM from HW.
All codecs, scaling, calibration and logic lie outside the IO variants and run identically in simulation, in SIL and on the target.
The root ports stay in place in HW (terminated or grounded), so the same model still compiles inside the top model.

The simulation-only parts are never deployed: `RC_Link_Sim`, `CAN1_Net_Sim`, `Link_MCU_GNC`, `Shaddad_SensorModels`, `Sim_Monitors`, `Viz_Logging` and the whole of `Shaddad_Plant` (including `Electronics_Plant`).

blocks.text: **Status.** With `VC_TARGET = 1`, `Shaddad_BMS` and `Shaddad_Companion` update without errors. `Shaddad_MCU` is blocked only by the missing STM32CubeCLT. Every build (ERT, STM32 board, SIL, PIL, External mode) is **BLOCKED, not failed**: Simulink Coder is licensed but not installed, and STM32CubeMX/CubeCLT and the GNU Arm tools are missing (D31). The Phase 1 demonstration in this report therefore runs entirely with `VC_TARGET = 0`.
Project and file structure

The MATLAB project `Shaddad_UGV.prj` sets the path and registers `scripts/shaddad_startup.m` as its startup file. When the project opens, startup creates `P`, `Ts`, `P_meta`, `VC_*`, the 88 `Bus_*` objects and the `cs_*` configuration sets, creates the MPC object `mpcRowObj` when `VC_ROW_TRACKER == 1`, and prints a product and tool report. Scripts generate the models: each of the 8 models and the 117 subsystem and library files is written by one of the 39 build scripts `scripts/build/build_*.m`. {fig:F33_project_structure.png} and {tab:tab_folders_arch} show the folder layout.

Do not edit the generated `.slx` files by hand, because the next build overwrites the changes. Change the build script `scripts/build/build_<name>.m` instead and run it again. Before you rebuild any part of the MCU model, read the warning in {sec:ch08_user_manual/Regenerating models}.
